root_cause.text: `gso_features_check()` in `net/core/dev.c` directly dereferenced the IPv4 header with `ip_hdr()`/`inner_ip_hdr()` to read `iph->frag_off`, but on PF_PACKET-injected SKBs those header offsets were not guaranteed to point to safely accessible linear data, leading to uninitialized/unsafe header access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `struct iphdr *iph = skb->encapsulation ? inner_ip_hdr(skb) : ip_hdr(skb);` with `skb_header_pointer(skb, nhoff, sizeof(_iph), &_iph)` and changes the check to `if (!iph || !(iph->frag_off & htons(IP_DF)))`, explicitly stating that direct dereference via `ip_hdr()/inner_ip_hdr()` is unsafe on packets injected from PF_PACKET paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TCPv4 GSO feature checking to safely read the IPv4 header from skbs and avoid using mangle-id features when the header is unavailable or not DF-marked.
intent_record.what: In the TCPv4 GSO feature check, the code no longer directly takes an IP header pointer from `inner_ip_hdr(skb)` or `ip_hdr(skb)`. Instead, it computes the network-header offset with `skb_inner_network_offset(skb)` or `skb_network_offset(skb)`, fetches the header via `skb_header_pointer()` into a temporary `struct iphdr _iph`, and adds a null-check so the DF-bit test is only performed when the header is successfully read.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the DF-bit inspection safer for skbs whose IP header may not be linearly accessible in memory. If the header cannot be accessed, or if the packet is not marked with IP_DF, the code disables `dev->mangleid_features`, preventing use of ID-mangling features when the IPv4 header cannot be reliably examined.

grouping_result.intent: Fix TCPv4 GSO feature checking to safely read the IPv4 header from skbs and avoid using mangle-id features when the header is unavailable or not DF-marked.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause in gso_features_check() by making IPv4 header access safe on SKBs and avoiding dereferencing header data when it may be unavailable, which matches the unsafe ip_hdr()/inner_ip_hdr() access issue.

This statement begins the unsafe selection of the IPv4 header pointer used later for dereference. The bug stems from using a header pointer derived from skb state without first ensuring the header is safely accessible.
